question: Add one line to the project section of ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so that every agent drafting paper text, beats, bullets or table notes reads writeup/style/voice.md first?

solvers.answer: Yes: one pointer line (not an @import of the guide) after the 'Writing-process reference' line, covering generator-written notes, subagent prompts and an exclusion for the author's text (A4).
Yes: one line in the form of the three existing project lines, citing the author's 29 Oct V6 words, limited by A4 (author text untouched) and A2 (no restyling outside the edit at hand).

Yes, if the line is scoped by action and file (applied deliberation outcomes included), excludes the author's and coauthors' text, and cites the author's answer to this item rather than an invented quote.

final_answer:
Yes. After the author's yes, back up C:/Users/james/.claude/CLAUDE.md to a dated copy and insert this line as a new bullet after the 'Writing-process reference' bullet (line 77) of the project section 'harxhar-0dte-professor (paper)':

answer_short: One line in your CLAUDE.md so every agent that writes paper text reads your style guide (writeup/style/voice.md) first; it waits for your yes.
rationale: All three lenses answer yes on checked grounds: the guide exists because the author asked for the V6 rule today, no mechanism loads it, agent text already carries the tail it bans, and the design the author adopted says the guide is loaded by every agent. Confidence 0.85: the yes is likely; the residual doubt is the mechanism (he might prefer a repo-level rule file) and the wording. T3 only because a CLAUDE.md change is a config hard trigger. Importance HIGH although the touches are process and wording: the line decides whether the author's own rule reaches the drafting of the introduction, abstract and headline sentences, and he asked for that rule today (PROTOCOL section 6, when unsure choose HIGH). Consequence 3: it governs future drafting in many places but changes no paper text now.

default: Nothing in CLAUDE.md changes. Agents read the style guide only when their task prompt names it; the coordinator names it in the drafting prompts it sends, which needs no config change.
alternatives: A rule file in the repo (.claude/rules/) that loads the guide whenever an agent opens a paper file: loads more reliably, but it is a new kind of config file that git ignores here; the fallback if agents ignore the pointer
No CLAUDE.md change, the coordinator names the guide in each drafting prompt: misses fresh sessions that apply your chat edits
Copy or import the whole guide into CLAUDE.md: about 70 lines in every session of every project, and two copies that drift apart
A repo-level CLAUDE.md: splits your project rules across two places and is committed separately on each branch
